clue.text: Fork in byway, initially leading to farm

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter is used
something leading to another goes in front of it, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: the first letter of byway
a ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle

explanation.surface: Directions to a farm: take the fork in the little side road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fork in byway' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Fork'; 'in' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a point where a road or river divides into separate ways, which is a fork.

clue.text: Free antelope and most of other ruminants

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little of it, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a buck is a male antelope or deer
sheep chew the cud, like antelope

explanation.surface: An offer of an antelope and most of a flock of other grazing animals for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKSHEE is British slang, originally military, for something given at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshee is informal British slang meaning without charge, gratis.

clue.text: In sacred river, a leading character

blocks.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star actor found swimming in a holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran' is a famous line from Coleridge's Kubla Khan, and crosswords use it often.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is the character that leads all the others.

clue.text: Piece of furniture - can it be baroque?

indicators.note: baroque style is elaborate and twisted, so the preceding letters get rearranged ornately

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An antiques buyer wonders whether a piece of furniture could be from the Baroque period.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, a standard item of household furniture.

clue.text: Ducks in shopping area by a road close to ponds

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a mall is a shopping centre
taken as written
Rd is the standard abbreviation for road
the last letter of ponds

explanation.surface: Ducks wander into a shopping centre beside a road near some ponds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like it means near, but it asks for the end letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallards are the commonest wild ducks, the green-headed drakes seen on park ponds.

clue.text: In a straight line? Amazing cartwheels, if so

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing or bewildering, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gymnast does wonderful cartwheels, provided they travel straight across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes 'if so', so every word after 'Amazing' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by the most direct route, measured in a straight line rather than along roads.

clue.text: Broad-minded, artist included in false statement?

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a libel is a published false and damaging statement
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Is it a lie to call an artist tolerant and open-minded?
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person is tolerant of views and behaviour different from their own, which is being broad-minded.

clue.text: Vote loser, possibly, for president

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters can be reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who loses an election might yet be in the running for president.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironic, since both Roosevelts won the presidency; Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected four times.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Legislative body established around North America and Spain

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word wraps the next item

blocks.note: set as in settled or fixed in place
the standard abbreviation
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A lawmaking assembly founded in North America and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrapping takes in North America only; Spain is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is the upper house of a parliament, as in the United States Congress, so it makes laws.

clue.text: Football club's team had to chill out

indicators.note: chilling out means unwinding, so the preceding letters are loosened into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A football club's players were told to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chill out' reads as one phrase, but 'chill' is part of the fodder and only 'out' signals the shuffle. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham Athletic is an English professional football club from Oldham, near Manchester.

clue.text: Potential shown by former PM's gardener

blocks.note: capability means potential ability
Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister 2007-2010

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's gardener shows real promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Capability Brown got his nickname from telling clients their estates had 'capabilities'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the great 18th-century English landscape gardener of country estates.

clue.text: Sat out in front of a Parisian church, being hearty

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the preceding letters are reshuffled
in front of fixes the order, putting the earlier parts ahead of the later ones

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
un is French for a
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone sits outside a church in Paris, in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means sturdy and wholehearted in loyalty, matching hearty in the sense of vigorous and robust.

clue.text: Boy nicking article is serious

indicators.note: nicking is stealing, so the boy takes in the article and holds it inside

blocks.note: a boy's name
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boy who steals is in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, which puns on the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and intensely serious in manner or purpose.

clue.text: Estimator abroad in Asian country

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A quantity surveyor working overseas in an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: East Timor (Timor-Leste) is a small nation in Southeast Asia, occupying the eastern half of Timor island.

clue.text: Highly curious after crime? Sounds like it in place of worship

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second in the answer
sounds like says the result is heard rather than spelt, so the pieces are matched by their sound

blocks.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
agog means eagerly curious

explanation.surface: Eager curiosity after a wrongdoing, perhaps from a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'sin agog' sounds like SYNAGOGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is the building where a Jewish congregation meets for prayer and religious instruction.

clue.text: Song told a story

blocks.note: first meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert
second meaning: said something untrue

explanation.walkthrough: 'Told a story' is the euphemism for fibbing, not narrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Lied is a German romantic song set to a poem, and also the past tense of lie, to say something false.

clue.text: Object after silly sketch

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a comic sketch is a short act

explanation.surface: Someone protests after a foolish comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a positional instruction but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made item, especially one of historical interest, so an object.

clue.text: Queen featured in Cuban newspaper

indicators.note: featured in says the answer appears within the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A queen makes the pages of a Havana daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714, the last Stuart monarch.

clue.text: Almost stop by nearby pen

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: to end is to stop
close means near

explanation.surface: Nearly coming to a halt beside a nearby animal enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as a noun, a writing tool, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen animals is to shut them in, which is to enclose them.

clue.text: Set-to with crew, unfortunately, in Northants town

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: set-to, a fight, used as letters
used as letters

explanation.surface: A rowing crew gets into a scrap in a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is short for Northamptonshire, an English county; Towcester is known for its racecourse. 'with' only joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a small market town in the English county of Northamptonshire.

clue.text: Given a ring and hired?

blocks.note: first meaning: betrothed, with an engagement ring
second meaning: taken on to work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a ring' also suggests a phone call, the line being busy, a third sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means promised in marriage, and also employed, as when a firm engages a lawyer.

clue.text: Stale pork pie, say, could be past its sell-by date?

definitions.text: pork pie, say, could be past its sell-by date

blocks.note: first meaning: out of date, hackneyed

blocks.clueFragment: pork pie, say, could be past its sell-by date
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a pork pie is a flat-crowned style of hat, and one that has passed its best

explanation.surface: A pork pie gone off in the fridge, well past its date.
explanation.walkthrough: The pork pie is not food but a pork pie hat, a flat-topped brimmed hat; an aged one is literally an old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something tired and unoriginal, which is stale in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Good one in bar, clear

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the Roman numeral for one
in Britain your local is your nearby pub

explanation.surface: Someone at a good table in the bar has a clear head.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning is clear and coherent, following sensibly from one step to the next.

clue.text: Big eel wriggling across lake, clear

indicators.note: wriggling suggests twisting about, so the letters are reordered
across means spanning or straddling, so the jumbled letters stretch around the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A huge eel swims across a lake whose water is crystal clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Legible handwriting or print is clear enough to be read easily.

clue.text: Spree in Crosby, perhaps ending in Bootle

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

blocks.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner
the last letter of Bootle

explanation.surface: A wild night out in Crosby that ends in Bootle.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby and Bootle are neighbouring towns on Merseyside, near Liverpool, so the surface is a local pub crawl; but Crosby here is Bing Crosby, the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive indulgence, especially in drinking, much like a spree.

clue.text: The minutes of the last meeting should be one of the most important things to be discussed?

definitions.text: The minutes of the last meeting should be one of the most important things to be discussed

blocks.clueFragment: one of the most important things to be discussed
blocks.note: surface reading: the minutes are a vital matter that must be debated

blocks.clueFragment: The minutes of the last meeting
blocks.note: setter's reading: approving the previous minutes is literally among the first items listed for any meeting

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a priority, but minutes of the previous meeting are near the top of any agenda list simply by custom, not importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being a top priority, and also literally being listed near the top of a meeting's list of business.

clue.text: Film ambassador and bishop on board train

indicators.note: on board means inside a vehicle, so the first pieces travel within the last word

blocks.note: HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
B is the chess notation for bishop
to train someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: A film about an ambassador and a bishop travelling on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is a verb here, not the railway the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beach is a 2000 film starring Leonardo DiCaprio, based on Alex Garland's novel.

clue.text: Around noon, notice vet coming

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the last word wraps the single letter

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A notice says the vet is visiting around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around noon' reads as a time, but 'Around' is the wrapping signal and noon supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is an arrival, especially of something important, so it means a coming.
